title: UNF Tapping Profile Dataset
verification_method: Hole-preparation (tap drill) values are derived by direct reference from the existing verified unf_threads dataset. Thread engagement and tapping process parameters have not been independently verified and currently carry no verification method. T2.1 obtained ISO 2306:1972's own inch-thread drill tables (Tables 3/4, metric drill diameters recommended for tapping UNC/UNF threads) and compared them against this dataset's existing inch-decimal values for the 3 sizes present here. The two sources diverge by up to ~0.09mm (different standard/convention: this dataset's values follow the US customary number/letter/fraction drill-series convention, while ISO 2306 recommends continuous metric drill diameters via its own nominal-minus-pitch approximation). This is a classified different_standard conflict, not an error — see audit/t2-1-tap-drill-numeric-verification.json. No existing value in this dataset was changed or promoted based on ISO 2306; the two are recorded as distinct, non-equivalent recommendations. T2.1a expanded this dataset to 8 total UNC / 7 total UNF records (previously 3 each), closing the coverage gap identified by T2.1's target seed set. The 5 (UNC) / 4 (UNF) newly added records were built from newly-verified base-thread identity data in unc.seed.json/unf.seed.json (see those datasets' new records' `provenance` blocks) rather than by copying ISO 2306 values into this dataset's existing US-customary convention. Every record in this dataset (old and new) now also carries a structured `iso_2306_alternative_drill` field — ISO 2306's own metric drill-diameter recommendation for the same thread, recorded as a distinct, separately-labeled, independently-verified value, never merged into or replacing `hole_preparation`. T2.2 established the full mathematical model for thread engagement (radial percentage vs. axial length, both formulas, and an explicit finding that no Tier-1 source supports 75% as a required/verified target) -- see docs/architecture/thread-engagement-model.md. No thread_engagement field on any record in this dataset was populated as a result; the model documentation exists independently of any per-record value.
license_notes: Hole-preparation values are re-derived from BoltLab's own already-reviewed unf_threads dataset; no copyrighted standards tables are reproduced. No new external source material was introduced in this phase.

This is NOT a correction to hole_preparation above and must not be merged, averaged, or treated as more/less authoritative than it.

derived_candidates.description: General mathematical relationship between pilot-hole (tap drill) diameter and resulting thread engagement percentage for 60-degree unified/ISO thread forms, commonly documented in general machining references (e.g. Machinery's Handbook) and widely reproduced in manufacturer tap-drill charts. This is the mathematical relationship only; it does NOT establish or endorse any specific target engagement percentage (e.g. 75%) as a BoltLab-verified recommendation, and 75% engagement is commonly cited by third-party tap-drill charts as the general-purpose target for standard UNC/UNF tap drill tables, but this specific figure has not been independently confirmed in this phase against a Tier 1 primary source and is not asserted as verified.
derived_candidates.source: general engineering reference (Machinery's Handbook); not attributed to a specific BoltLab-verified standard record
derived_candidates.note: Recorded for reference only, as general methodology context per Section 8 of the T2 phase brief. No target_engagement_percent field on any tapping_profile record has been populated using this formula.
